NONE: › informal for
debutante
› a complete failure, especially because of bad planning and organization
（尤指因計劃和組織不周而導致的）徹底失敗，一敗塗地，崩潰

example: The collapse of the company was described as the greatest financial debacle in US history.
那間公司的破產被稱為美國歷史上最大的一場金融災難。

NONE: › to stop someone from doing something by law or by official agreement
（透過法律或協議）禁止，阻止

example: He was debarred from the club for unacceptable behaviour.
他因行為不檢而被禁止進入俱樂部。

NONE: › to reduce the quality or value of something
使墮落；貶低
› to lower the value of a coin by making it from a less valuable metal
（透過摻雜非貴重金屬）降低硬幣的價值

example: Some argue that money has debased football.
有人說金錢腐蝕了足球運動。
Our world view has become debased. We no longer have a sense of the sacred.
我們的世界觀墮落了，我們不再具有神聖感。

NONE: › not clear or certain because different people may have different opinions
具爭議的，不確定的；成問題的

example: [ + question word ] It's debatable whether a university degree helps at all.
大學學位是否有用是一個具爭議的話題。
The value of some of the experiments is debatable.
有些實驗的價值還有待確定。

NONE: B2 (a) serious discussion of a subject in which many people take part
談論，討論；爭論，辯論

I or T: C2 [ I or T ] to discuss a subject in a formal way
T: › [ T ] to try to make a decision about something

example: Education is the current focus of public debate.
教育是目前大眾談論的焦點。
How we proceed from here is a matter for debate.
我們還需要討論下一步該怎樣做。
Over the year we have had several debates about future policy.
一年來，我們就未來的政策進行了幾次討論。
In Parliament today, MPs debated the Finance Bill.
今天在議會上議員們討論了財政法案。
They had been debating for several hours without reaching a conclusion.
他們已經爭論了好幾個小時，仍然沒有得出一個結論。
[ + question word ] The authorities debated whether to build a new car park.
政府有關部門就是否要修建一座新停車場進行了討論。
[ + question word ] We debated whether to take the earlier train.
我們考慮到底要不要乘早一點的那班列車。
I'm still debating what colour to paint the walls.
我還在考慮要把牆刷成甚麼顏色。

NONE: › to destroy or damage something so that it is no longer considered good or moral
使變壞，使敗壞

example: Lenin said that the best way to destroy the capitalist system was to debauch the currency.
列寧說，摧毀資本主義體系的最好辦法是擊垮其貨幣。

NONE: › made weaker or destroyed by bad sexual behaviour, drinking too much alcohol, taking drugs, etc.
糜爛的，放蕩的；沉湎酒色的；嗜毒的

example: his debauched lifestyle
他那種糜爛的生活方式

NONE: › bad sexual behaviour, drinking too much alcohol, taking drugs, etc.
道德敗壞；淫蕩；沉湎酒色（或毒品）

example: a life of debauchery
糜爛的生活

NONE: › a type of loan, often used by companies to raise money, that is paid back over a long period of time and at a fixed rate of interest
（公司）債券
› to make someone or something physically weak
使虛弱；削弱，使衰弱

example: Chemotherapy exhausted and debilitated him.
化療使他感到非常疲憊虛弱。

NONE: › physical weakness
體虛，虛弱
B2 (a record of) money taken out of a bank account
借項
B2 to take money out of an account or keep a record of this
借記

example: The account was in debit at the end of the month (= more money had been spent than was in the account at that time).
月底帳面出現入不敷支。
Debits are shown in the left-hand column.
借方紀錄展示在左邊一欄裡。
The bank debited my account.
銀行從我的帳戶上扣去了錢。
The bank debited the money from my account.
銀行從我的帳戶上扣去了錢。
The unauthorized borrowing fee will be debited to your account.
未經許可的借貸費用會記在你的帳上。

NONE: B2 a small plastic card that can be used as a method of payment, the money being taken from your bank account automatically
（銀行存款戶持有的）轉帳卡

example: I paid with my debit card.
我用轉帳卡付了款。

NONE: › the list of numbers that shows amounts of money that have been spent from a bank account
借方欄，支出記錄，支出賬目
› (especially of men) attractive, confident, and carefully dressed
（尤指男人）有魅力的，明亮照人的，風度翩翩的

example: a debonair appearance/manner
明亮照人的形象／富有魅力的舉止
a debonair young man
風度翩翩的年輕人

NONE: › a treatment in which dead tissue is removed from wounds such as burns in order to help them get better
清創術

example: chemical debridement
化學清創術

NONE: › to question someone in detail about work they have done for you
詳細詢問，盤問（執行任務的情況）

example: The pilots were thoroughly debriefed after every mission.
機師每次完成任務後，都要接受詳細詢問。
a debriefing session
執行任務情況匯報會

NONE: › broken or torn pieces of something larger
碎片，殘駭

example: Debris from the aircraft was scattered over a large area.
飛機殘駭散落在一片很大的區域。

NONE: B2 something, especially money, that is owed to someone else, or the state of owing something
借款，欠款；債務

example: He managed to pay off his debts in two years.
他設法在兩年內還清債務。
The company ran up huge debts.
公司很快就負債累累。
They are in debt to (= owe money to) the bank.
他們欠銀行的錢。
He got into debt (= borrowed money) after he lost his job.
他失業後開始舉債。
The company is deep in debt (= owes a lot of money).
公司已經債臺高築。

NONE: › the situation in which a bank or a government tells a person, a company, or a government that they do not have to pay back the money they owe
債務免除（銀行或政府告知個人、公司或政府不需償還借款）

example: There are plans to provide full debt relief for some African countries.
有些計畫對一些非洲國家提供完全債務免除。

NONE: › someone who owes money
借方；負債者，債務人

T: › to remove bugs (= mistakes) from a computer program
› to look for and remove bugs (= hidden listening or recording devices) from a place

example: to debug a program
排除程式中的錯誤
Security officers had debugged the room before the meeting.
保安人員在開會前已檢查房間，以防有人安放竊聽裝置。

NONE: › to show that something is less important, less good, or less true than it has been made to appear
駁斥；揭穿，揭露…的真相

example: The writer's aim was to debunk the myth that had grown up around the actress.
作者的目的是為了揭穿圍繞這位女演員的種種傳聞。

NONE: C1 the occasion when someone performs or presents something to the public for the first time
首演，首次公演
› to perform or be introduced to the public for the first time
首演，首次登臺；首次亮相

example: She made her professional stage debut in Swan Lake.
她在《天鵝湖》中完成了她的首次職業舞臺演出。
her debut (= first) album
她的首張專輯。
The Broadway show debuted last year to great acclaim.
這個百老匯節目去年首次演出就受到了廣泛讚揚。

NONE: › a rich young woman who, especially in the past in Britain, went to a number of social events as a way of being introduced to other young people of high social rank
（尤指舊時英國）初次踏足社交界的上流社會年輕女子

example: a debutantes' ball
初次在社交舞會露面
